metaDescription: Eureka corded upright vacuums compared by weight, brush roll design, lift-up pods and dust cup size, so you match a PowerSpeed or FlexReach to your home.
expertTake: The Eureka FlexReach NEU651PL is the most versatile upright here because the pod lifts away and the brush roll resists hair wrap. The PowerSpeed NEU182B is the value pick: light, simple and with a big cup. Skip the family for allergy-heavy homes that need a published sealed system; these are plain bagless uprights.
introParagraphs: This maker's uprights are built around being light. Most weigh far less than a full-size family upright, which makes them easy to carry up stairs and store in a closet, at the cost of smaller motors and simpler filtration.

The range splits into ultra-light budget models, mid-weight PowerSpeed machines and newer designs with a detachable pod. The questions that matter are how much the machine weighs, how it handles hair and whether the brush roll can be switched off for hard floors.

products.name: Eureka FlexReach NEU651PL lift-away upright, anti-tangle

specList.label: Type
specList.value: Corded bagless upright with detachable pod

products.description:
FlexReach is the model that makes an upright flexible. A one-step release lifts the main canister off the base so you can carry it and use the hose for stairs, upholstery and ceiling corners, and an anti-tangle multi-surface roll is built to prevent hair wrap on the floor. LED headlights and swivel steering finish a package aimed at a house with pets and furniture.

Next to the PowerSpeed NEU280 it adds the pod and the anti-tangle roll, which are the two features most owners wish they had. The maker calls it its flagship power with flexible reach, a positioning claim and not a measurement.

The pod joint is the part to keep clean. Wipe the release mechanism and its seal every month, rinse the filters and let them dry, and check the roll for hair at the ends even with the anti-tangle design. Keep the hose free of kinks when you store it, since a bent hose cracks over a year of use. When you carry the pod by its handle, hold the hose clear of the floor and keep the cord out of the way, because a hose end that drags across the carpet picks up grit that scores the inside of the wand. Lift the pod gently back onto its cradle until the latch clicks, since a half-seated pod is the commonest reason owners report a sudden loss of suction after reassembly.
products.bestFor: Pet homes with stairs and furniture that want one machine for everything.
pros: Lift-up pod for stairs and furniture
cons: Pod joint is an extra seal to keep clean

products.name: Eureka MaxSwivel Pro NEU350 with switchable brush roll

specList.label: Brush roll
specList.value: Manually controllable, can be turned off

products.description:
The manual brush roll control is the feature that matters on mixed floors. You can switch the roll off on tile and hardwood so it stops flicking crumbs and scuffing a polished plank, and on again for carpet. A dual cyclone system handles larger debris and finer dirt together, and LED headlights light the path.

Compared with the FlexReach it has no pod and no anti-tangle roll, so hair wrap is more likely, but it is the better pick for a home with a lot of hard floor. Swivel steering lets it turn around furniture without lifting.

Check the brush roll for hair every few weeks and rinse the filters on schedule. Remember to switch the roll back on before you cross a rug, since a roll left off on carpet cleans poorly and many owners mistake that for a weak motor. A good habit is to glance at the switch every time you change rooms, and if the household shares the machine, put a small label on the handle as a reminder. The headlights help here too, because you can see at once whether the roll is spinning when you tilt the head back, which is the quickest check before you start a rug.
products.bestFor: Homes with a lot of hard floor and a few rugs.
pros: Brush roll can be switched off for hard floors
cons: Plain brush roll can wrap hair
Easy to forget the roll setting

products.name: Eureka PowerSpeed NEU280 with upgraded cyclone system

specList.label: Cyclones
specList.value: Upgraded cyclone system for larger debris

specList.label: Use
specList.value: Pet hair, carpet and hard floor

products.description:
The NEU280 is the PowerSpeed with a new cyclone system that the maker says handles larger debris, such as cereal and cat litter, that earlier models struggled with. It stays lightweight and penetrates carpet to extract embedded dirt.

Next to the NEU182B it is a newer design with a cyclone upgrade, while the older model has the larger cup. If your floors see a lot of chunky debris, the cyclone upgrade is the reason to prefer this one.

Empty the cup before it reaches the line, rinse the filter and check the roll for hair. A cyclone design works best when the dirt it separates is not allowed to build against the filter side, so do not wait until the cup is packed. Chunky debris such as cat litter and cereal is also hard on the roll bearings and the belt, so check for a stuck piece under the roll cover when you hear a rattle, and avoid running the machine over small hard objects like coins or screws, which can lodge in the nozzle and jam the roll before the cyclone ever gets a chance to separate them.
products.bestFor: Homes with chunky debris and carpet that want a light upright.
cons: No pod or wand conversion listed

products.name: Eureka PowerSpeed Anti-Tangle E2, 960W, 12 lb
products.description:
The E2 sells itself on not cutting hair off the roller: the brush roll is described as actively preventing wrap, and a 960 watt motor delivers consistent suction from hardwood and tile to area rugs. At about 12 pounds it is easy to carry up stairs and room to room.

Compared with the NEU280 it adds the anti-tangle roll and a bigger motor figure, but it weighs more. The 960 watt rating is the electrical input, so read it as a motor size and not as a cleaning result.

Check the bearing ends of the roll for the odd strand, rinse the filter monthly and empty the cup. A lightweight upright tips easily, so park it standing against a wall. At 12 pounds it is still light enough to carry one-handed, but the cord is the part that wears, so coil it loosely on the hooks instead of wrapping it tightly around the handle, and never pull the plug out by the cord. If you find the motor sounding strained, look first at the cup and the filter before you suspect the motor, since a packed cup is far more common than a motor fault.
products.bestFor: Pet homes that want to stop cutting hair off the roller.
cons: Wattage is not a cleaning result

products.name: Eureka Airspeed NEU10AE5, 7.7 lb quick-release handle
products.description:
At about 7.7 pounds the Airspeed is the lightest upright in the family, which is the whole point. A quick-release handle lets you use it for above-floor cleaning with the crevice tool or the dusting brush, and it extracts dirt and hair from hard floors and carpets.

It is a modest machine, so thick carpet and large homes are beyond it, but it is a good second vacuum for a flat or for a person who struggles to lift a heavier upright. Next to the E2 it is far lighter and weaker.

Empty the small cup often, rinse the filter and check the roll for hair. A very light upright needs a gentle touch on rugs, since pushing hard can tip it. Because there is so little weight pressing the head into the carpet, the machine relies on the brush roll to do the work, so go slowly over rugs and make overlapping passes rather than quick strokes, and keep the cord behind you so the thin body does not tangle in it. As a second vacuum for a bedroom or an upstairs hall, a very light machine like this earns its place.
products.bestFor: Small homes and users who need the lightest upright.
pros: Crevice tool and dusting brush included

products.name: Eureka PowerSpeed NEU182B, 10 lb, 2.6L dust cup

specList.label: Use
specList.value: Carpet, shag rug and hard floors

products.description:
The NEU182B pairs a 10 pound body with a 2.6 liter dust cup, which is big for a light upright, and five height adjustments for carpet, shag and hard floors. The dynamic motor and brush roll lift heavy debris, according to the maker.

It is the older sibling of the NEU280 and the NEU181D, so it lacks the cyclone upgrade, but the cup is bigger and the price is low. Next to the E2 it has a larger cup and a plain roll.

Tip the 2.6 liter cup out at the fill line, rinse the filter and set the height for the floor. Adjusting the height matters on rugs, because a head set too low drags and a head set too high leaves dirt. The big cup makes a heavy bin when it is full of sand or garden soil, so empty it at about two thirds full and tip it into a bag held close to the opening, and wash the cup in warm water now and then, letting it dry completely before refitting so that no damp film traps fine dust on the walls.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want a light upright with a big cup.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Airspeed NEU10AE5 weighs about 7.7 pounds, the NEU182B about 10 and the E2 about 12. Weight decides how often you carry the machine upstairs and whether it feels light in the hand. Choose the lowest weight that has the power you need, and keep in mind that a light machine feels lighter still on a rug than on bare floor, so test your choice against the floor you clean most often rather than the stairs you climb once a week, which is the opposite of what most buyers do.

The FlexReach and E2 use anti-tangle rolls, the NEU350 allows the roll to be turned off and the others have plain rolls. Hair wrap is the main chore on any upright. Choose by the hair in your home and the floors you have, and recognize that an anti-tangle design usually means softer agitation, so a heavy carpet may be cleaned a little less deeply, while a roll that you can turn off is the right answer for a house that is mostly wood or tile.

The FlexReach lifts the canister away for stairs and upholstery, which the others cannot do. A pod adds a seal to keep clean. If you clean above floor often, it is the feature worth paying for, since it removes the need for a second machine and lets you reach stair treads, curtains and the car with the same suction you use on the floor, rather than a weaker handheld.

The NEU182B has a 2.6 liter cup, big for a light upright, while the Airspeed's is small. A small cup forces frequent stops. Match the cup to your mess, and remember that a larger cup is heavier when full, so a household that wants a light machine should empty it more often, and a household with big pets and a lot of carpet should prefer the bigger cup despite the extra weight.

The NEU280 has an upgraded cyclone for larger debris, and the NEU350 has a dual cyclone system. Cyclone design affects how well the filter stays clean. Tip the cup out ahead of a packed load so the cyclone keeps working.

None of these lists a published sealed system. Treat the filters as basic, wash them regularly and empty the cup outdoors. For allergies, choose a sealed bagged model from another maker, and in the meantime wash the filters often, empty the cup outdoors and keep the vacuum off carpet that the allergic person sleeps on until it has been cleaned and aired.

cards.label: Ultra-light
cards.text: The Airspeed and NEU182B are easy to carry and store but have small motors and basic features.

cards.label: Mid-weight
cards.text: The E2, NEU350 and FlexReach weigh more and give you anti-tangle rolls, roll control or a pod.

howToChoose.note: Choose ultra-light for a flat, mid-weight for a house.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A detachable pod or a quick-release handle and a low weight.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The FlexReach pod lifts away, and the Airspeed handle releases for above-floor cleaning.

cards.text: You have a small home. The Airspeed or NEU182B does the job.

maintenance.why: Hair wraps the roll and strains the belt.
A clogged filter cuts suction. Dry fully.
A packed cup cuts cyclone separation.

A worn belt stops the roll and the machine then pushes dirt around instead of lifting it. A belt is a cheap part, so replace it at the first sign of slipping and keep a spare in the closet with the manual.
Lint on the seal leaks airflow.

faq.a: The FlexReach NEU651PL is the most versatile, with a detachable pod and an anti-tangle roll. The NEU182B is the value pick, with a big cup and a low weight, and the Airspeed is the one to buy if lightness is the only thing that matters.

faq.q: Are Eureka uprights good for pets?
faq.a: The E2 and FlexReach have anti-tangle rolls. Others can wrap long hair.

faq.q: Can I turn the brush roll off?
faq.a: On the MaxSwivel Pro NEU350, yes. That protects hard floors, stops crumbs from scattering and spares delicate finishes, though you must remember to switch it back on before you cross a rug.
The Airspeed is about 7.7 pounds, the NEU182B 10 and the E2 12.

None lists a sealed system. Wash filters regularly, and do not assume that a filter described as HEPA media is the same as a sealed system, since the seal around the housing is what stops fine dust from bypassing it.

faq.q: Are these good for thick carpet?
faq.a: Light motors work best on low and medium pile. Thick carpet favors heavier uprights, because weight presses the head into the pile and helps the brush roll agitate deeply, and a very light machine can skim over a shag rug without lifting what lies beneath, however clean the surface looks afterward.
